**Finding submitted: compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment.

There was no substantive defect to repair across either round of feedback. The verifier confirmed each element of the analysis and attributed the sole failure to the `audit frequency limited` deterministic check, which it described as explainable heuristic noise in a document with no audit clause. I therefore held the classification and tightened the rationale so it leads with the direction of the rule and disposes of the failing check explicitly.

The position, in short:

- **Kubient holds no audit right.** Searches for *audit*, *records*, *inspect*, *verif* returned nothing, confirmed by a full read of the agreement's single section.
- **Neither near-candidate qualifies.** §5 (p0023) grants no examination or true-up right; §1 (p0001) obliges AP only to cooperate so Kubient can deliver the Services.
- **Better than preferred.** No audit right means no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure to cap.
- **Compliant, not missing.** "Missing" would require drafting an audit obligation against our own client — contrary to the rule's protective purpose.
- **Parked, not double-flagged.** The absence of an AP-side check on Kubient-measured Impressions is a gap that runs *in our favour*, so it belongs to the reporting/revenue-verification rule.

One practical note for the deal team: because the deterministic check for this rule can never pass on a document that contains no audit clause, this finding will keep surfacing as a red check on re-runs. It is worth suppressing or whitelisting that check for no-clause-present outcomes so the signal isn't mistaken for an unresolved gap.
